about: Recall cues Claude actually issued in the saga1 run (harness family-saga), each with the memories that existed at that moment and, labelled by hand, the ones that answer the cue. Empty relevant = nothing should come back.

queries.cue: quantities plain floats vs decimal/fraction type, why

m00001.text: format_qty shows quantities as kitchen fractions (denominators 2,3,4,8, snapped only within 1e-6) else as up to 2 decimals with trailing zeros stripped; we never approximate e.g. 0.3 to 1/3 because that would change the amount.

m00002.text: parse_line accepts unicode vulgar fractions (½, 1½, 1 ½) and U+2044 fraction slash via unicodedata; an attached whole part must be ASCII digits

m00003.text: units.normalize only strips a plural -es/-s when the result is a known unit (glasses->glass, cups->cup); unknown words pass through unchanged. glass/pinch/dash are 'count' units: they parse but convert() refuses them by design.

m00004.text: parse_line reads a leading 'a'/'an' as qty 1 only when a unit follows, and drops a linking 'of' after the unit ('a pinch of salt' -> 1 pinch salt).

m00005.text: convert(qty, frm, to, ingredient) crosses volume and mass only via GRAMS_PER_CUP (US cup, spoon-and-level, exact name or alias match, no fuzzy); salt deliberately excluded because kosher vs table salt differ about 2x

m00006.text: The canonical example 'a pinch of salt' parses cleanly but is unconvertible twice over: pinch is a count unit and salt is excluded from GRAMS_PER_CUP.

m00007.text: Shared design principle: never fabricate precision. format_qty refuses to snap 0.3 to 1/3, and convert refuses fuzzy density matches and salt, so either way the code prefers exact output or refusal over plausible approximation.

m00008.text: The leading 'a'/'an' rule depends on units.dimension recognising the next word (after plural stripping), so 'a lemon' keeps qty 0 and 'a lemon' as text, while 'a glasses of water' yields 1 glass water.

m00009.text: Both describe deliberate refusals in convert(): count units and salt are excluded on purpose, not by omission.

m00010.text: Parse and format are asymmetric: parse_line accepts any unicode vulgar fraction, but format_qty only emits denominators 2,3,4,8, so an input like ⅕ or ⅙ comes back as a decimal (0.2, 0.17).

m00011.text: The lemon is a citizen of the ingredient field; the Devanagari two is a citizen of nowhere.

m00012.text: Where does it stop holding: 'a 1/2 cup' (article then number), 'a few cups', or nouns that collide with known units such as 'a can of beans' or 'a clove' if those are registered units?

m00013.text: Does it hold for full-width digits ('１½'), mixed '1⁄2' with ASCII around U+2044 after an attached whole ('1 1⁄2'), doubled glyphs ('½½'), or negative quantities?

m00014.text: 1e-6 is the width of the plural s.

m00015.text: Where does 'never approximates' stop being true: the 2-decimal fallback itself rounds (1/6 shows as 0.17), and a value like 1.9999995 snaps to 2.

m00016.text: Does it hold for irregular plurals ('leaves', 'loaves'), abbreviations ending in s ('lbs', 'tbs'), mixed case ('Cups'), or a unit whose singular itself ends in s?

m00017.text: The salt cellar has two padlocks and a note saying 'ask grandma'.

m00018.text: Stops being true if a specific salt (e.g. 'table salt' or 'diamond crystal kosher salt') is added to GRAMS_PER_CUP, or if pinch ever gains a volume definition.

m00019.text: The principle already bends: format_qty's 2-decimal fallback rounds 1/6 to 0.17, a display approximation the code tolerates. It holds for the amount's identity, not for every printed digit.

m00020.text: [imagined experiment] Where can salt be weighed?: Both padlocks hold today. GRAMS_PER_CUP has 16 entries and no salt; 'salt', 'kosher salt' and 'table salt' all raise ValueError 'no density known'. pinch and dash raise 'cannot convert pinch to tsp' even to another volume unit, so a pinch has no volume definition at all, not merely no density. The only way salt gets weighed is inside butter: 'salted butter' (any case) aliases to butter and converts at 227 g/cup. (ran it: Read-only python3 -I import of recipe_core.units (no bytecode written): convert(1,'cup','g',X) for salt, kosher salt, ta) Surprise: Salt is convertible only when it is dissolved in butter. Also, ingredient lookup is case-insensitive ('Salted Butter' works), which no memory recorded. Verdict: delightful.

m00021.text: Add a test pinning that 'salt' raises while 'salted butter' converts, so the alias table can't accidentally swallow salt.

m00022.text: Record as a memory that ingredient lookup in units.density is case-insensitive.

m00023.text: If someone adds salt, it will arrive as named varieties (e.g. 'table salt' ~ 290 g/cup, 'diamond crystal kosher salt' ~ 135 g/cup) and bare 'salt' will stay unaliased; a test asserting convert(1,'cup','g','salt') raises will be the guard.

m00003.text: units.normalize only strips a plural -es/-s when the result is a known unit (glasses->glass, cups->cup); unknown words pass through unchanged. glass/pinch/dash are 'count' units: they parse but convert() refuses them by design.

m00004.text: parse_line reads a leading 'a'/'an' as qty 1 only when a unit follows, and drops a linking 'of' after the unit ('a pinch of salt' -> 1 pinch salt).

m00005.text: convert(qty, frm, to, ingredient) crosses volume and mass only via GRAMS_PER_CUP (US cup, spoon-and-level, exact name or alias match, no fuzzy); salt deliberately excluded because kosher vs table salt differ about 2x

m00006.text: The canonical example 'a pinch of salt' parses cleanly but is unconvertible twice over: pinch is a count unit and salt is excluded from GRAMS_PER_CUP.

m00007.text: Shared design principle: never fabricate precision. format_qty refuses to snap 0.3 to 1/3, and convert refuses fuzzy density matches and salt, so either way the code prefers exact output or refusal over plausible approximation.

m00008.text: The leading 'a'/'an' rule depends on units.dimension recognising the next word (after plural stripping), so 'a lemon' keeps qty 0 and 'a lemon' as text, while 'a glasses of water' yields 1 glass water.

m00009.text: Both describe deliberate refusals in convert(): count units and salt are excluded on purpose, not by omission.

m00010.text: Parse and format are asymmetric: parse_line accepts any unicode vulgar fraction, but format_qty only emits denominators 2,3,4,8, so an input like ⅕ or ⅙ comes back as a decimal (0.2, 0.17).

m00011.text: The lemon is a citizen of the ingredient field; the Devanagari two is a citizen of nowhere.

m00012.text: Where does it stop holding: 'a 1/2 cup' (article then number), 'a few cups', or nouns that collide with known units such as 'a can of beans' or 'a clove' if those are registered units?

m00013.text: Does it hold for full-width digits ('１½'), mixed '1⁄2' with ASCII around U+2044 after an attached whole ('1 1⁄2'), doubled glyphs ('½½'), or negative quantities?

m00014.text: 1e-6 is the width of the plural s.

m00015.text: Where does 'never approximates' stop being true: the 2-decimal fallback itself rounds (1/6 shows as 0.17), and a value like 1.9999995 snaps to 2.

m00016.text: Does it hold for irregular plurals ('leaves', 'loaves'), abbreviations ending in s ('lbs', 'tbs'), mixed case ('Cups'), or a unit whose singular itself ends in s?

m00017.text: The salt cellar has two padlocks and a note saying 'ask grandma'.

m00018.text: Stops being true if a specific salt (e.g. 'table salt' or 'diamond crystal kosher salt') is added to GRAMS_PER_CUP, or if pinch ever gains a volume definition.

m00019.text: The principle already bends: format_qty's 2-decimal fallback rounds 1/6 to 0.17, a display approximation the code tolerates. It holds for the amount's identity, not for every printed digit.

m00020.text: [imagined experiment] Where can salt be weighed?: Both padlocks hold today. GRAMS_PER_CUP has 16 entries and no salt; 'salt', 'kosher salt' and 'table salt' all raise ValueError 'no density known'. pinch and dash raise 'cannot convert pinch to tsp' even to another volume unit, so a pinch has no volume definition at all, not merely no density. The only way salt gets weighed is inside butter: 'salted butter' (any case) aliases to butter and converts at 227 g/cup. (ran it: Read-only python3 -I import of recipe_core.units (no bytecode written): convert(1,'cup','g',X) for salt, kosher salt, ta) Surprise: Salt is convertible only when it is dissolved in butter. Also, ingredient lookup is case-insensitive ('Salted Butter' works), which no memory recorded. Verdict: delightful.

m00021.text: Add a test pinning that 'salt' raises while 'salted butter' converts, so the alias table can't accidentally swallow salt.

m00022.text: Record as a memory that ingredient lookup in units.density is case-insensitive.

m00023.text: If someone adds salt, it will arrive as named varieties (e.g. 'table salt' ~ 290 g/cup, 'diamond crystal kosher salt' ~ 135 g/cup) and bare 'salt' will stay unaliased; a test asserting convert(1,'cup','g','salt') raises will be the guard.

m00024.text: Quantities have always been plain floats (never Fraction/Decimal); float error is handled at display time by format_qty's 1e-6 kitchen-fraction snap. A 'switch back to floats for speed' request rests on a false premise; answered in README Design notes.

queries.cue: which day does the week start, Monday or Sunday

m00001.text: Shopping list merges same item across compatible units: one unit used -> kept as written; any metric input -> ml/g, switching to l/kg at >=1000; all imperial -> largest used unit giving >=1. Unconvertible units (None, clove) merge only with the same normalized unit.

m00002.text: planner/units.py normalize() is vendored from recipe-core and crashes on None and strips any trailing 's' (e.g. 'glass'->'glas'); shopping.py guards None itself rather than patching the vendored copy.

m00003.text: Shopping quantities are summed exactly with fractions.Fraction (floats read via str, so 0.5+0.2 cup = 0.7 exactly) and rounded to 2 decimals only at output; render lines with shopping.format_line(), never str() of the raw number.

m00004.text: plan_week always plans Monday..Sunday of the week containing start (default today); an explicit start date is a reference day and snaps back to its Monday, never used as a literal first day.

m00005.text: Household defaults to 2 (planner.week.HOUSEHOLD); a recipe with serves >= 2x household is cooked once and the following night(s) are leftovers entries ({'leftovers': True, 'cooked_on', 'recipe', 'ingredients': []}); shopping_list skips leftovers so nothing is bought twice; rotation advances on cooking nights only; leftovers never spill past Sunday.

m00001.text: Expiry is counted in local calendar days (date subtraction), never timedelta.days or utcnow(): those made tomorrow's milk read 0 days at 11pm and hid yesterday's expired items.

queries.cue: distance units km miles preference conversion

m00001.text: Pace is formatted by trail.log._fmt_pace: round total seconds per km first, then divmod by 60 and zero-pad (m:ss); never split minutes from a float fraction.

m00002.text: Distances are formatted only at display time by trail.log._fmt_distance as 'X.XX km (Y.YY mi)' (2 decimals, miles = km / 1.609344 exact); distance_km()/distance_miles() stay raw floats for maths.

m00003.text: Elevation gain filters GPS jitter: centred moving average over 100 m of track distance (SMOOTH_WINDOW_M), then low-to-peak hysteresis with 8 m threshold (GAIN_THRESHOLD_M); simple ratchet hysteresis was rejected because it drops the sub-threshold tail of each climb; threshold-only or smoothing-only both let noise through at sigma 2-3 m. Documented in README 'Elevation gain'.
